text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any recent injury to that finger, or has this developed gradually without a specific cause?

text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of pain and inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint, combined with the resting extension, strongly suggest a disruption at the extensor tendon insertion. Can you confirm if you are currently unable to actively extend the tip of your finger? REQUEST TEST: Hand_Special_Exams (Extensor Mechanism Assessment)

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent injury mechanism and your inability to actively extend the tip of your finger are highly concerning for an extensor tendon rupture. I have requested a specific exam to assess the extensor mechanism; please confirm if you have a "drop finger" deformity where you cannot straighten the distal joint without help. REQUEST TEST: Hand_Special_Exams (Extensor Mechanism Assessment)

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rupture of the Extensor Mechanism (Jersey Finger) at the Distal Interphalangeal Joint.

The combination of the forced flexion injury, your inability to actively extend the distal phalanx, and the classic "drop finger" deformity confirms a rupture of the extensor tendon insertion. This is a surgical emergency requiring immediate immobilization and referral to orthopedic surgery.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
